metadata.title: Nasdaq futures slip on chip weakness; S&P 500 holds gains

content.text:
By Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi
Nov 5 (Reuters) - Nasdaq futures dropped on Thursday as chip and data center-related stocks remained under pressure, while S&P 500 contracts extended gains slightly from the last session following the Democrats' sweeping midterm election victory.
Qualcomm dropped 9.6% in premarket trading after the chipmaker fell short of Wall Street estimates for fourth-quarter smartphone chip sales on sluggish demand and declining Apple-related revenue.
Broader semiconductor stocks extended losses after Wednesday's fall, with Nvidia down 0.8%, Marvell Technology off 3.4% and Intel slipping 2%.
Chip stocks, along with companies linked to the AI infrastructure buildout, slipped further following the Democrats' election victory including in some key data-center states, where public opposition to the industry's rapid expansion has been growing.
"Data center pauses will slow the pace of buildout into 2028 with ~30% of expected 2028 additions now at risk of being impacted," UBS strategists said in a note.
"The slowdown is a negative for Semis and AI infrastructure, but a lot is already priced into Semis with valuations nearing multi-year lows."
Data center operators IREN, Hut 8, and Applied Digital fell between 1.1% and 2.7%. Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius Group fell 3% each.
Utilities and equipment suppliers exposed to the data center boom, including GE Vernova and Constellation Energy, were also trading lower. AI server maker Dell was down 2.9%.
Most large-cap tech stocks meanwhile built on their gains from the last session as a slower AI buildout was seen as helping them.
Amazon.com, Meta Platforms and Alphabet were up above 1%.
Elon Musk-led SpaceX and Tesla were down over 1% each, extending losses. Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars backing Republican candidates, including efforts to keep them in control in Texas, the home state of both companies.
At 7:04 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were up 330 points, or 0.62%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 15.5 points, or 0.2%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 145.5 points, or 0.51%.
The S&P 500 clocked its biggest one-day percentage gain in three months on Wednesday as the easing political uncertainty boosted risk appetite.
Some analysts said that a divided government in Washington could lead to fewer sharp legislative changes and may even make it harder to agree on fiscal spending, given the US's deteriorating fiscal picture.
A sharp drop in oil prices in the previous session had also supported the sentiment. Brent crude futures were up over 1% on Thursday after dropping more than 8% on Wednesday.
